Build a keyframe animation from a plot

Source: R/animate.R
animate.Rd

animate() compiles a plot carrying a transition_states() into one keyframe scene per state, training the scales once over all states and freezing them, and returns a vellum_animation. Write it with anim_save(); printing it shows the first keyframe as a preview.

Usage

animate(
  plot,
  nframes = 50,
  fps = 25,
  start_pause = 0,
  end_pause = 0,
  rewind = FALSE
)

Arguments

plot

A PlotSpec with a transition_states() (and optionally an ease_aes()).

nframes

Total number of frames to render, a positive whole number. The pauses and the rewind are part of it, as in gganimate.

fps

Frames per second (the playback rate written into the file).

start_pause, end_pause

Number of frames to hold the first and the last frame for, before the animation starts and after it ends (default 0). A looping file (every format loops) then rests on the final picture before starting over: end_pause = fps holds it for a second.

rewind

Play the animation backwards after it has played forwards, so the loop returns to its start smoothly instead of cutting (default FALSE). The frames are split between the two directions; the end pause sits between them and the start pause at both ends.

Value

A vellum_animation.

Details

Per-state statistics (e.g. a smooth) are recomputed per keyframe, but no scale domain retrains — the frozen scales are the observable proof the animation stayed non-reactive (axis breaks do not move between frames).

Which mark becomes which

Marks tween by identity, as gganimate matches by group: each mark of one state moves into the mark that is the same thing in the next state, however the rows are ordered and whatever groups each state contains. A mark's identity is

  1. its data_id, when the layer declares one (mark_point(data_id = country)): the way to follow individual observations;

  2. otherwise its group – the group aesthetic if mapped, else the combination of the layer's discrete mapped aesthetics (color, fill, shape, ..., and a discrete x, y or label) – so a bar race's bars, filled by country, slide between ranks keeping their colours;

  3. and within a group, the order of its rows – the last resort, enough when each group has one mark per state, but rows of one group pair up by position. Give such a layer a data_id (or a group) when its rows are individual observations whose order may change.

A line, path or area is one mark per series and is matched by its group.

A faceted plot animates panel by panel: every panel of the whole data is drawn in every frame (a state without rows for a panel leaves it empty rather than dropping it), and a mark's identity includes its panel, so a mark never slides from one panel into another – a row whose facet value changes between states fades out of one panel and into the other. The scales are frozen across frames, so per-panel scales (facet_wrap(scales = "free"), an independent resolve_scale()) are refused.

A mark found in only one of two adjacent states fades in or out (points, bars and tiles, labels, lines and areas alike, with their effect underlays such as glow()) on the alpha easing, and a point whose colour group changes slides to its new place while its colour blends. A line, path or area whose number of points changes morphs from one outline into the other. Where marks overlap, the stacking order switches to the next state's halfway through the transition. What cannot move switches whole halfway through: decoration without an identity that comes and goes, or a line that cannot be morphed (a broken line with missing values, mixed units). animate() warns (once per call) when that will happen, naming the states.

Give each transition enough frames to be seen: nframes is spread over all the states, so 40 states in 80 frames leave two frames per state and nothing visibly moves.

Frame variables

A title, subtitle or caption (set with labs()) may embed frame variables in braces, glue-style, as in gganimate: labs(title = "Year: {frame_time}"). Each {...} is an R expression evaluated per frame with the variables below in scope (and the environment animate() was called from behind them), so "{round(frame_time)}" or "{format(frame_time, '%Y')}" work; write {{ and }} for literal braces. The label is updated on every frame, not only at keyframes: a {frame_time} title counts through the in-between times while the marks move.

  • every transition: frame (the frame number), nframes, progress (frame / nframes);

  • transition_states(): closest_state, previous_state, next_state (the state the frame is nearest to, comes from and goes to; all three are the held state during a pause) and transitioning (TRUE while moving). closest_state switches halfway through a transition, on the position easing, when the marks' discrete attributes do;

  • transition_time(): frame_time, the time the frame has reached (on the position easing, so it agrees with where the marks are), of the time column's class (Date, POSIXct, or double);

  • transition_reveal(): frame_along, the along value revealed so far.

A mark_text() label can use the same variables (VP-93): mark_text(data = data.frame(x = 3000, y = 40), x = x, y = y, label = "{round(frame_time)}", size = 60) draws the year large behind a gapminder bubble chart, counting on every frame. A constant label or a column of labels may contain {...}; the label is placed (and moves) as the mark it belongs to, and only its string changes per frame. Repelled and rich-text labels are not templated. An ordinary data label whose string differs between two states takes the nearer state's string, switching halfway through.

Pauses and rewind

start_pause and end_pause hold the first and last frame for that many frames, and rewind = TRUE plays the animation back to the start, as in gganimate. They come out of nframes: animate(nframes = 100, end_pause = 20) moves for 80 frames and rests on the final picture for 20. Every output honours them – anim_save() to GIF, APNG or SVG, anim_frame()'s frame numbers, and the frame scrubber of an animated vellumwidget.

See also

transition_states(), ease_aes(), anim_save(), anim_frame()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Four bars in every state, so each bar tweens into its next height.
d <- data.frame(t = rep(1:3, each = 4), g = rep(letters[1:4], 3),
                v = c(1, 3, 2, 4, 4, 1, 3, 2, 2, 4, 1, 3))
vplot(d) |>
  mark_bar(x = g, y = v, fill = g) |>
  transition_states(t) |>
  animate(nframes = 60, fps = 25)
} # }
